rows.headcount_source_title: HHS Fact Sheet — Transformation to Make America Healthy Again
rows.headcount_quote: The Department has 82,000 full-time employees... HHS will reduce its full-time employee count from 82,000 to 62,000 (a reduction of approximately 20,000).
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Department-wide weighted avg: heavy clinical (IHS) and lab/field (CDC) lower the mix, but large knowledge-work blocs (NIH researchers, CMS adjudicators, FDA reviewers, ASTP/AHRQ analysts) pull it up.
rows.notes: Pre-RIF headcount used as ~80k (FY24 baseline). 2025 reductions are in flight; budget documents still cite ~80k FTE. Excludes contractors.

rows.headcount_quote: CMS' Program Management account supports approximately 6,700 full-time equivalent (FTE) staff.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: CMS workforce is overwhelmingly knowledge work (policy, regulation, claims/payment program oversight, actuaries, IT). Clinical reviewers are a minority subset (~0.55 rubric), but the bulk of HQ FTE are admin/policy.
rows.notes: CMS administers ~$1.5T but employs a small FTE base; relies heavily on contractors (MACs).

rows.headcount_quote: NIH employs approximately 20,000 staff including scientists, physicians, and administrative personnel across 27 Institutes and Centers.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Intramural researchers ARE LLM users (per rubric ~0.85). Even clinical NIH staff (Clinical Center, ~1,200) are heavy data/literature workers. Bench scientists, program officers, grants management — all knowledge work.

rows.headcount_quote: CDC employs more than 13,000 staff in 50 states and over 60 countries.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Lab + epi staff (~0.75 per rubric). Field epidemiologists, lab scientists, and surveillance analysts all do heavy data/literature work amenable to LLM assistance.
rows.notes: Includes Commissioned Corps officers; ~75% knowledge-work eligible per rubric.

rows.headcount_source_title: FDA at a Glance — Fact Sheet
rows.headcount_quote: FDA's staff of approximately 18,000 employees includes physicians, microbiologists, chemists, statisticians, and other scientists.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Reviewers (CDER/CBER/CDRH) are document-heavy knowledge workers (~0.85). ORA field inspectors (~5k) are mixed (~0.40). Weighted ~0.75.

rows.headcount_quote: HRSA's FY 2025 request supports approximately 2,700 FTE.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Grants administration, policy, program oversight — knowledge work throughout. Few clinical or field staff.

rows.headcount_quote: IHS provides comprehensive health service delivery... with approximately 15,500 employees, including Commissioned Corps officers and civil service personnel.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Clinical workforce dominates (per rubric ~0.15, like VHA). Tribal health programs are direct-care.
rows.notes: Many additional staff at tribally-operated facilities are not federal IHS FTE.

rows.headcount_quote: ACL's FY 2025 request supports approximately 200 FTE.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Small policy/grants agency. Almost entirely knowledge work.
rows.notes: ACL was reorganized in 2025; FY25 baseline FTE ~200.

rows.headcount_quote: ACF employs approximately 1,500 staff administering programs including Head Start, TANF, and child welfare.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Grants administration, policy oversight, program management. Knowledge work throughout.

rows.headcount_quote: AHRQ's FY 2025 request supports approximately 300 FTE.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Research agency staffed by PhDs, data scientists, policy analysts. Heavy LLM-eligible per rubric.

rows.headcount_quote: ASPR has approximately 1,100 employees coordinating national preparedness and response.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Policy/coordination knowledge work, but includes deployable medical response teams (NDMS) and SNS logistics roles — pull share slightly below pure-HQ baseline.

rows.headcount_quote: SAMHSA's FY 2025 budget supports approximately 900 FTE.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Grants and policy agency; clinical functions are at grantees not in-house. Knowledge work throughout.

rows.headcount_quote: ASTP/ONC is the principal Federal entity charged with coordination of nationwide efforts to implement and use the most advanced health information technology; staff approximately 200.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Tech-policy office of standards, interoperability, and health-IT certification staff. Effectively all knowledge work.

rows.headcount_quote: The Department of Justice employs approximately 115,000 attorneys, agents, correctional officers, and support staff.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Weighted down by FBOP (~35k correctional officers, ~0.10), FBI agents in field (~14k, ~0.25), and ATF/DEA/USMS sworn (~16k combined, ~0.30). Knowledge-work blocs: USAO attorneys, DOJ litigation divisions, OJP.
rows.notes: FBOP alone accounts for ~30% of DOJ FTE.

rows.headcount_quote: The FBI employs more than 38,000 people, including special agents, intelligence analysts, language specialists, scientists, information technology specialists, and other professionals.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: ~14k special agents in field (~0.25 per rubric); ~24k analysts, IT, lab, support staff (~0.55+). Weighted ~0.40.

rows.headcount_quote: ATF employs approximately 5,300 people, including special agents and industry operations investigators.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: ~2.6k special agents (~0.30 per rubric); industry operations investigators and lab/admin staff (~0.50). Weighted ~0.35.

rows.headcount_quote: DEA employs approximately 9,500 personnel, including more than 4,600 Special Agents.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: ~4.6k special agents (~0.30 per rubric); diversion investigators, intelligence analysts, lab chemists, admin (~0.50). Weighted ~0.35.

rows.headcount_quote: The U.S. Marshals Service has approximately 5,500 employees including Deputy U.S. Marshals and Criminal Investigators.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Majority sworn deputies/criminal investigators in field operations (~0.25); HQ/admin and intelligence analysts (~0.55). Weighted ~0.30.

rows.headcount_quote: The Federal Bureau of Prisons employs approximately 35,000 staff who supervise about 155,000 federal inmates.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Correctional officers dominate (~0.10 per rubric); some HQ policy, training, and health-services staff lift slightly.

rows.headcount_quote: The Bureau of Justice Statistics is a small statistical agency with approximately 60 employees.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Federal statistical agency — almost entirely statisticians, data scientists, analysts. Highly LLM-eligible.

rows.headcount_quote: EOIR has more than 3,400 employees including immigration judges, Board members, attorneys, and support staff at headquarters and immigration courts nationwide.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Immigration judges, BIA attorneys, law clerks, court staff — predominantly legal knowledge work.

rows.headcount_quote: OJP has approximately 800 employees managing grants and providing leadership to support state, local, and tribal justice systems.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Grants administration, policy, research (NIJ, BJS, BJA, OJJDP, OVC). Knowledge work throughout.

rows.headcount_quote: The Antitrust Division has approximately 850 attorneys, economists, paralegals, and support staff.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Attorneys + PhD economists — knowledge work per rubric (~0.85+). High litigation document load.

rows.headcount_source_title: Offices of the U.S. Attorneys — About
rows.headcount_quote: The 93 U.S. Attorneys' offices employ approximately 11,500 attorneys and support staff.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: Federal prosecutors, civil division attorneys, paralegals, support — virtually all knowledge work.
rows.notes: USAO (DOJ slug doj-eousa = Executive Office for U.S. Attorneys, covering all 93 districts in aggregate).
